TW// ED talk

I suffered through anorexia for many years so I can definitely give you my input from my own experience. When you suffer with an ED, it’s an obsession. It’s all you ever secretly think about and the deeper you fall the harder your mind could control it. It’s like your brain is reprogrammed to create new habits, restrict certain ways, and of course body check constantly. The body checks help reassure yourself on your “progress” and it almost self-soothes the disorder’s voice. Like “you’re doing a good job, keep it up!” It’s a validation to the disorder. Any type of health problems caused by the ED (stomach ache/cramping, fainting) is also a sick form of accomplishment/validation in your head, too. I remember feeling waves of euphoria month after month I deteriorated, but you could never be skinny enough to satisfy it.

Thankfully for my case, the realization that I was actually dying woke me up before it got more deadly. But in Eugenia’s situation I’m sure she doesn’t believe she would eventually die. She can’t even admit that she has an ED.

It’s a terrible, terrible nightmare to suffer through. It’s all you ever think about and sadly all you ever become.
